chunks: Look, how they were when their groups were united, their views were unanimous, their hearts were moderate, their hands used to help one another, their swords were intended for assisting one another, their eyes were sharp and their aims were the same,
Did they not become masters of the corners of the earth and rulers over the neck of all the worlds?

Thereafter, also see what happened to them towards the end when division overtook them, unity became fractured, and differences arose between their words and their hearts. They divided into various groups and were scattered fighting among themselves.

Then Allāh took away from them the apparel of His honour and deprived them of the prosperity produced by His favours. Only their stories have remained among you for the guidance of those who may learn the lesson from them.
ai.seo_question: What lesson does Imam Ali draw from the rise and fall of the Umayyads in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) utilizes the historical trajectory of the Umayyads as a paradigmatic case study in *Nahj al-Balagha*, illustrating how the accumulation of worldly power without spiritual grounding leads to inevitable fragmentation. This passage serves as a critical theological warning against *al-hawa* (capricious desire) and the loss of *karama* (divine dignity), emphasizing that political dominance is transient when internal cohesion and divine favor are lost.
